item.title: LIV Golf lays off many of its employees as it prepares for second iteration with new investors
item.description: LIV Golf informed employees their jobs will end in early September as PIF funding concludes and the league transitions toward a new LIV 2.0 era.
item.content:encoded:
LIV Golf has informed many of its employees that their employment will end beginning the first week of September. As LIV alluded to in a statement, the mass layoffs do not come as a surprise following the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) announcing that it would stop funding the circuit at the conclusion of the 2026 season.

LIV Golf's 2026 campaign ended on Aug. 23 in Indianapolis, although the conclusion came a week early after the Team Championship in Michigan, slated for the end of August, was canceled earlier this month.

"The funding commitment announced by PIF earlier this year will reach its conclusion. As a result, we are scaling back operations as we transition to the next chapter of LIV Golf and work toward making LIV 2.0 a reality," a LIV Golf spokesperson shared.

WYNDHAM CLARK ADDRESSES CHEATING ALLEGATIONS AFTER BEING ACCUSED OF IMPROVING LIE DURING BMW CHAMPIONSHIP WIN

"This week, we informed many of our colleagues that their employment under LIV 1.0 will end in the first week of September. We are grateful to our employees for their hard work and dedication in building LIV Golf, and we remain committed to supporting those affected through this transition."

LIV leadership continues to be optimistic that the league will continue in 2027, calling it a new 'LIV 2.0' version, while it is also hopeful that many of the employees soon to be laid off can return.

LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil announced on Aug. 5, ahead of the circuit's event at Trump National Bedminster, that a new investor had been secured, and a term sheet had been signed. Specific details of the investor have yet to be announced.

"LIV Golf has an agreement in place with a lead investor, signed by the investor and approved by the Board, to anchor the transaction and play a key role in supporting the path forward for the League’s next era, driven by and for the players," O'Neil said at the time.

What is known regarding LIV 2.0 is that players competing in the league will hold a majority of equity. Also, the reported plan for the 2027 LIV schedule is for it to feature 10 events, with five in the United States and five across the globe.

item.title: Democrat officials charged for allegedly scamming COVID relief funds
item.description: Two Democratic Party officials in Massachusetts face federal indictments alleging they schemed to steal over $700,000 in COVID relief funds.
item.content:encoded:
Authorities arrested a Democratic Party official for alleged COVID fraud for the second time this month on Wednesday.

U.S. Attorney Leah Foley says police arrested Massachusetts State Rep. Francisco Paulino early Wednesday morning, charging him with 11 counts related to pandemic unemployment insurance fraud, pandemic loan fraud, and money laundering.

"According to the Paulino indictment, Mr. Paulino devised a scheme to obtain more than $700,000 in federal pandemic relief funds. It is alleged that Paulino used some of the money for his own personal use, including real estate expenses, loan payments and transfers to his campaign account," Foley said.

"Other money he flipped around and lent to other individuals at higher interest rates than the pandemic loan rate," she continued.

11 SUSPECTED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS AMONG 15 ARRESTED IN $1.4M BENEFITS FRAUD CRACKDOWN IN MASSACHUSETTS, DOJ SAYS

The indictment says Paulino's alleged fraud began in 2020 when he signed up for COVID relief funding on behalf of "an unwitting 77-year-old relative."

Paulino's arrest comes roughly a week after the FBI arrested Lawrence Mayor Brian DePeña on similar charges. A federal grand jury also handed down an 11-count indictment against DePeña with charges relating to pandemic loan fraud and money laundering.

The FBI says DePeña first began "diverting public funds" in 2020 when he was serving on the Lawrence city council. He was arrested earlier this month.

MINNESOTA FRAUD MASTERMIND GETS NEARLY 42 YEARS IN PRISON IN MASSIVE $250M 'FEEDING OUR FUTURE' SCHEME

"Everyone listening today knows how difficult it was for Americans during the pandemic," Foley said. "The money these two individuals allegedly scammed was meant for hardworking Americans and struggling business owners, not for two greedy individuals who lied and stole for their own personal benefit."

"It is never a proud moment when we arrest a public official, but we will continue to do it until the message is received: No one is above the law, and no one gets a pass," she added.

item.title: Unlicensed Miami surgeon 'Dr. Frankenstein' vanishes days before trial over botched procedures: authorities
item.description: Joao Batista Cunha De Araujo's ankle monitor triggered a tamper alert days before his trial on 14 charges tied to unlicensed plastic surgery in Miami.
item.content:encoded:
A Brazilian national accused of performing plastic surgeries without a license in Miami has allegedly vanished days before he was set to go on trial for more than a dozen charges connected to theft, fraud and practicing medicine without credentials, according to authorities.

Joao Batista Cunha De Araujo, 57, dubbed "Dr. Frankenstein" by critics, faces 14 charges, 13 of them felonies, in Miami-Dade County, according to an arrest warrant reviewed by Fox News Digital. He was arrested after a pair of anonymous tips led authorities to conduct a sting at his office — an undercover detective went in for a consultation on chin liposuction and was allegedly given a quote for the procedure.

Miami-Dade authorities confirmed to Fox News Digital that Araujo surrendered his passport after a court order and was put on an ankle monitor while awaiting trial. Then he disappeared.

TEXAS MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING PREGNANT WIFE ALLEGEDLY CUTS OFF ANKLE MONITOR AND FLEES TO ITALY

Local authorities deferred questions about his whereabouts to the U.S. Marshals and the Brazilian government, neither of which could immediately be reached for comment.

According to court documents, Araujo's ankle monitor "generated a tamper alert" on Saturday, Aug. 1 — three days before the scheduled beginning of his trial.

TEXAS MAN ACCUSED IN PREGNANT WIFE'S MURDER FIGHTS TO REMAIN IN ITALY, CITING 'LIFESTYLE AND CULTURE'

Two officers responded to his last known location in a high-rise on the Bay Harbor Islands, just north of Miami Beach. They were unable to locate Araujo or the ankle monitor, and his house arrest was revoked and a Miami judge issued a new arrest warrant and authorized full extradition.

Araujo's attorney, Mark Eiglarsh, told Fox News Digital he was still looking at discovery in the case and that the trial date likely would have been pushed back.

"My client previously entered a plea of not guilty to the charges, and I was prepared to vigorously challenge the allegations brought by the prosecution," he said. "For reasons unknown to me, he has chosen to make himself unavailable to continue fighting for his innocence. If he ever reappears, I will continue to fight zealously on his behalf."

According to a New York Post report citing four sources close to the case, Araujo is believed to have left the country for his native Brazil — raising questions about how he did so after turning in his passport.

RUNAWAY BRAZILIAN EX-SPY CHIEF CONVICTED IN COUP REPORTEDLY DETAINED BY ICE AT FLORIDA TRAFFIC STOP

Araujo's wife and co-defendant Amanda Soares Felizardo Ungaro, 41, posted a video Wednesday that appears to show her husband smiling and sitting across from her at a restaurant table. It was not immediately clear when or where it was taken.

She faced seven charges in connection with the case against her husband and was deported earlier this year. She did not immediately respond to a message from Fox News Digital.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Araujo had previously asked the court to allow him to return to his home country while awaiting trial — a request Judge Tanya Brinkley denied amid concerns that he would not be able to return to Florida, court documents reveal.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

According to a police affidavit, the Florida Department of Health confirmed that neither Araujo or Ungaro had any kind of medical license in the state.

CALIFORNIA DOCTOR CONVICTED OF $45M MEDICARE FRAUD SCHEME THAT FUNDED LUXURY VACATIONS AND A $12K CROSSBOW

At least one patient suffered injuries from a botched procedure, according to court documents.

GOT A TIP?

A victim identified in court documents as "AJ" told police that she visited Araujo for some lip and jaw filler and was injected with 17 bottles in a single sitting.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

The filler hardened, leaving lumps in her lips, jaw and cheekbone.

She initially paid $15,000, according to the complaint, but the price was reduced to $7,000.

She went on to seek help from a licensed plastic surgeon.

item.title: Terrifying video captures people fleeing incoming mudslide at Nepal-China border
item.description: Video captures mudslides engulfing buildings in Gyirong, Tibet, minutes after a 4.4 magnitude earthquake triggered flash flooding near Nepal's border.
item.content:encoded:
A video taken after flash flooding on the border between Nepal and China shows mudslides enveloping multiple buildings as people fled in Gyirong, Tibet near China's border with Nepal.

The mudslides followed a 4.4-magnitude earthquake which occurred just seven minutes before video captured people sprinting away from the disaster, according to the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ).

Nepal's foreign minister Shishir Khanal also suggested that earthquakes could be the cause in remarks to the country's parliament, according to Reuters.

COLOMBIA BUILDING COLLAPSES ON CAMERA AS EARTHQUAKE BRINGS DEATH, DESTRUCTION

Authorities believe the earthquake caused an ice-rock avalanche which flowed into the Lhende Khola River in Nepal, according to Reuters.

At least 95 people have been confirmed dead as rescue authorities in Nepal have recovered at least that many bodies.

Nepal's tourism authority said at least 484 tourists have also been reported missing, at least three of whom are U.S. citizens.

Reports claim as many as several dozen more Americans are missing. No official count of Americans has yet been released by the U.S. government.

The U.S. State Department said it was monitoring the situation closely and communicating with authorities in Nepal.

"The Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans," a State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"The State Department is aware of Americans impacted by the floods in Nepal and is closely tracking the situation. The Embassy is working closely with local tour agencies and local authorities to assist Americans in the affected areas. We extend our deepest condolences for the victims and to the families of all those affected," the statement continued.

"We strongly encourage U.S. citizens in the affected areas to monitor local news, follow the emergency instructions provided by local authorities, and enroll in STEP.state.gov to receive important emergency information," the spokesperson added.

The State Department's office of Consular Affairs also relayed travel advisories for specific areas within Nepal.

"The flood destroyed buildings and damaged roads, bridges, electricity infrastructure, and communications. Nepali authorities ordered people living along riverbanks and in low-lying areas to move to safer locations," the department posted on X.

"Avoid travel on the Prithvi Highway, the Galchhi–Nuwakot–Rasuwa–Syafrubesi road, and the Mugling–Narayangadh road until authorities lift restrictions. If you are in Rasuwagadhi, Timure, Syafrubesi, Langtang, or another affected area, contact the U.S. Embassy when safe to do so and provide your name, location, and status," the advisory read.

MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF

Sixty-five people are being treated at hospitals in and around Nepal's capital Kathmandu, according to local officials.

Authorities also warned that a second flood is possible as there is still a blockage lodged on the Lhende Khola River.

33 RESCUED FROM VENEZUELAN RUBBLE: SURVIVAL WINDOW DESPERATELY FADING WITH NEARLY 50,000 MISSING

China deployed 574 rescuers to Tibet's Gyirong land crossing, though one rescuer told CCTV that it would take hours to reach the deluged site, Reuters reported.

India's government and the European Union (EU) have publicly offered support to Nepal and China.

US MILITARY DEPLOYS MTVRS, AIRLIFTS AID TO VENEZUELA FOLLOWING DEADLY EARTHQUAKES

"Spoke to Prime Minister Balendra Shah and conveyed condolences on the loss of lives due to the floods in Nepal. The people of India stand in solidarity with their sisters and brothers in Nepal at this difficult time. India is ready to provide all possible humanitarian assistance to Nepal. Our teams are coordinating closely on rescue and relief efforts," Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi wrote in a post on X.

Shah responded on X, calling Modi's gesture "a reflection of the enduring bonds of friendship between our two countries, which we profoundly value."

"Devastating floods have struck communities in Nepal and China. My thoughts are with all those affected, especially the families who have lost loved ones or are still waiting for news... Copernicus has been activated to help map the affected areas in Nepal and support the response on the ground. We stand ready to mobilise further European assistance," European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen also wrote on X, offering up the use of Copernicus, the EU's Earth monitoring satellite program.

Fox News Digital also contacted Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs for more information.

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Teen planned middle school massacre before making deadly ‘last-minute choice’ to kill mom: official
item.description: Lilyana Wagner, 16, pleaded guilty to killing her mother after abandoning plans for a school shooting, listing six shooters in her confession.
item.content:encoded:
A teenage Georgia girl was convicted of brutally killing her mother after abandoning a plan to commit a school shooting, following an obsession with mass casualty events, authorities said.

Lilyana Rose Wagner, 16, was sentenced to life in prison after pleading guilty to murder and aggravated assault in the November 2024 death of her mother Rachel Wagner, 51, Tifton District Attorney Patrick Warren said Tuesday.

The slaying was discovered after Wagner, then 14, crashed her mother's car. Wagner told responding officers that she lived alone with her mother.

The officers went to the home to perform a welfare check and discovered Rachel Wagner, who had not shown up for work and wasn't answering her phone, dead from a gunshot wound to the back of her head.

GEORGIA HIGH SCHOOL SHOOTING SUSPECT COLT GRAY CHANGES PLEA TO GUILTY, NOW FACES LIFE IN PRISON

Investigators found that the teenage Wagner had become obsessed with school shooters and mass shootings, developing an online and social media reputation as someone interested in planning and executing a mass casualty event.

In a handwritten confession, the teen described the decision to kill her mother instead.

"This whole thing was a last-minute choice," she wrote. "I was going to commit a school shooting at my old middle school but chose this instead. Although I didn’t commit a school shooting, the whole event was inspired by these people."

She then listed the names of six different school shooters from memory.

FATHER WHO BOUGHT AR-15 FOR GEORGIA SCHOOL SHOOTER LEARNS FATE IN FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND CONVICTION

In the months before the killing, officials said Wagner communicated via apps with anonymous people who encouraged her to plan and commit murder.

Investigators later found that Rachel Wagner had purchased the gun her daughter used at a pawn shop a month before the killing. She allowed the teen to keep the weapon and ammunition in her bedroom, prosecutors said.

In a statement, Warren warned parents to monitor the content their children view online.

FRANCE BECOMES FIRST EU NATION TO BAN SOCIAL MEDIA FOR CHILDREN UNDER 15

"I urge you to never underestimate the influence that exists behind your child’s screen," Warren said. "In the courtroom, I see the consequences after the messages and the online encouragement from strangers have already turned into real-world crimes."

"By then, remorse for your actions cannot erase the damage, and a prosecution cannot give victims back what was taken," Warren added. "It is your duty to know who is influencing your child, and it is your duty to know what they are being taught to believe is acceptable."

Lilyana Wagner will serve 30 years in prison before becoming eligible for parole.

item.title: Trump scores federal court win against House progressive accused of assaulting ICE
item.description: A Biden-appointed judge sided with Trump's DOJ, rejecting House Democrat LaMonica McIver's legislative immunity argument for getting her case thrown out.
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge appointed by former President Joe Biden is siding with the Trump administration in refusing to dismiss a case against a House Democrat accused of assaulting federal immigration officers.

Two of the three judges on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit refused to dismiss the Department of Justice (DOJ) case against Rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., stemming from a 2025 incident at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in Newark, New Jersey.

An unannounced visit to the Delaney Hall detention center by a group of Democratic officials devolved into chaos in May 2025 that culminated in a physical standoff between federal lawmakers and ICE agents and the arrest of Newark Mayor Ras Baraka. McIver was charged with three counts, including assaulting and impeding federal officers.

FIVE ANTI-ICE AGITATORS ARRESTED DURING CHAOTIC DELANEY HALL CONFRONTATIONS CAUGHT ON VIDEO

She attempted to get the case thrown out, arguing that she is immune from prosecution because her actions were part of her official duties as a member of Congress.

She also accused the DOJ of unfairly singling her out, with her congressional office calling the charges "vindictive."

DOJ VOWS TO APPEAL AFTER JUDGE DISMISSES SMUGGLING CHARGES AGAINST KILMAR ABREGO GARCIA AS 'VINDICTIVE'

But the 2-1 decision, made by Biden-appointed Judge Cindy Chung and Trump-appointed Judge Stephanos Bibas, stated that McIver's argument of legislative immunity would not stand for two of the three counts, while the third count was sent back to a lower court for further review.

Court documents say McIver allegedly "slammed her forearm" into a federal officer trying to arrest Baraka. On that count, the federal appellate court agreed with a lower court decision that her "alleged intervention into the Mayor’s questionable arrest had no cognizable connection to any legislative function" protected by the Constitution.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS LOST OR ABANDONED HUNDREDS OF LAWSUITS AGAINST ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS, MIGRANTS: REPORT

The second count alleged that McIver used both of her forearms to "strike [an officer] as she returned inside of the secured area of Delaney Hall."

The two judges wrote, "Like the acts charged in Count One, the acts of pushing past and forcibly striking someone are unambiguously non-legislative: they are not integral to the legislative process."

Judge Thomas Ambro wrote in dissent, "When an Executive Branch official prevents a Member from entering a DHS facility, she is denied effective access to an oversight inspection."

McIver herself said in a statement that "the court got it wrong."

"Today’s decision chills that authority and emboldens the Trump administration to continue persecuting our most vulnerable communities, those who try to defend them, and anyone who dares hold the president or his lackeys accountable. I will not fold to this administration. We are exploring every possible option. The administration will not stop me from doing my job or standing for what is right. This is not over," McIver said.

item.title: Watchdog demands apology after UN memorial erroneously honors Hamas terrorist
item.description: UN Watch says UNRWA teacher Imad Youssif El Samhouri glorified terrorism for years before the United Nations honored him at a memorial service.
item.content:encoded:
A solemn candle-lighting ceremony honoring United Nations employees who died in 2025 while working for the world body has sparked criticism after it unwittingly named an employee who was later revealed to be a Hamas commander.

At the annual memorial service in June honoring 136 employees who died in service to the U.N. in 2025, Secretary-General António Guterres, General Assembly President Annalena Baerbock, and then-Security Council President Leonor Zalabata Torres helped light a candle representing "an eternal flame." An official later read Imad Youssif El Samhouri’s name alongside those of other U.N. employees as a violinist played somber music.

El Samhouri was employed by the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) as a teacher and associate principal before becoming principal of UNRWA Rafah Preparatory Boys School B. On Aug. 8, Hamas identified El Samhouri through messaging site Telegram as a field commander in the Al-Qassam Brigades.

UN CHIEF BACKS OFFICIAL WHO REPOSTED ANTI-ISRAEL ACTIVIST'S CLAIMS AMID CALLS FOR INVESTIGATION

During the event, Guterres said that "more U.N. colleagues have been killed in Gaza than in any other conflict or disaster in the history of the United Nations. Some died alongside their families, in their homes, in the places they sought refuge. Others were killed while carrying out their duties in offices, in shelters, and in communities they served. These tragedies weigh heavily on us all and should be remembered by the entire world. Let me be clear. U.N. personnel must never be targeted."

Guterres also said, "In keeping with long-standing practice, we have sought the consent of families to read aloud the names of those we honor. Tragically, in the case of men who served with UNRWA, we could not reach those families because they, too, have been killed or forced to flee."

Hillel Neuer, executive director of UN Watch, has written an open letter to Guterres and Baerbock asking both to issue an apology for the incident and acknowledge that UNRWA is "unwilling or unable" to roust terrorists from its schools.

Stéphane Dujarric, spokesperson for Guterres, told Fox News Digital during a press briefing last week, "[UNRWA] and we are always very deeply concerned when allegations against the former staff is raised. Obviously, when his name was included, the agency was not aware. I will remind you that the list of all UNRWA staff is shared with the Israeli parties as they are every year. His name was shared in the list of 2024. No concerns were raised based on that information from the Israeli side, and obviously, had those allegations been raised before, his name would likely not have been included."

When pressed further about whether Guterres would retract the honors or issue an apology, Dujarric seemed to put the blame on Israel, "We're now stating our position, which makes it clear. Had we known, and had we been told, his name would probably not have been included."

Israel’s U.N. Ambassador Danny Danon told Fox News Digital, "It is outrageous to watch the U.N. spokesperson struggle to clearly condemn the crimes committed by former UNRWA employees. Israel repeatedly warned the U.N. that active Hamas terrorists were operating within UNRWA and played a significant role in the atrocities of Oct. 7. The U.N. spokesperson’s response reflects Secretary-General Guterres’ entire tenure: the organization has lost its moral compass. It is because of terrorists like Imad Youssif El Samhouri and others that Israel ended UNRWA’s operations in Israel."

Neuer has accumulated multiple social media posts that he says are attributed to El Samhouri, which demonstrate his support of so-called Palestinian martyrs, his praise for the kidnapping of Israeli teens, and his support for the "good news" of Hamas attacks between 2012 and 2014. 

El Samhouri’s case is one of about 200 cases that senior fellow at UN Watch Salo Aizenberg told Fox News Digital he has cataloged in which terror groups shared posthumous proof that journalists, NGO personnel, aid workers, lawyers and medical personnel were part of their organizations. Citing the Institute for Palestine Studies, which says El Samhouri was killed June 8, 2025, when Israeli forces targeted his tent with no warning, Aizenberg noted on X that El Samhouri was "using the cover of the humanitarian zone as a human shield" when he was targeted.

ISRAEL ACCUSES UN OF PLACING IT ON SAME SEXUAL VIOLENCE BLACKLIST AS HAMAS TERRORISTS, SEVERS TIES

In a martyr video viewed by Fox News Digital that the Israel Defense Forces provided, El Samhouri stands before multiple grenades and a weapon and states that "the call to arms has resounded in the hearts of the faithful and they have answered the call." He also says that "we have chosen jihad as our path; our anthem is that Death in the cause of Allah is our highest aspiration, and our resolve will not waver, no matter how long the road or how great the sacrifices." 

In the same video, while standing within what appears to be an underground tunnel, El Samhouri thanks God, "who has honored us with the tunnels and made them a means of resistance, a means by which the Zionist enemy never imagines we will emerge from beneath the ground."

Neuer told Fox News Digital, "Samhouri publicly glorified terrorism, circulated Hamas battlefield propaganda and brought Hamas officials into UNRWA school life. Photographs show his own principal, Muhammad Al-Bardawil, repeatedly appearing at school events with Jumaa Al-Ghoul, Hamas’ representative in Rafah." He said, "The evidence shows clearly that many officials in the UNRWA school system knew about Samhouri’s support for terrorism and ties to Hamas, and that they actually tolerated or even encouraged it."

item.title: Scottie Scheffler shares a perfectly imperfect assessment of work-life balance, the challenges of fatherhood
item.description: Scottie Scheffler opens up about the grind of raising two young kids while competing as the world's No. 1 golfer ahead of the Tour Championship.
item.content:encoded:
Scottie Scheffler is the No. 1-ranked golfer on Earth. He is also a husband and father to two children under the age of three. While that first fact about Scheffler is as unrelatable as they come, the second, the one that carries immense responsibilities and its own set of pressures, completely different from those he faces on the golf course, well, that's something millions can relate to.

Being a professional athlete, and in Scheffler's case, being the literal best in your respective sport, while also being a family man and raising kids, is one of those things we regular folk can't comprehend simply due to the fact that so few people on Earth experience such a thing.

SAM BURNS IS ONE OF AMERICA'S BEST GOLFERS, BUT FAITH, FAMILY AND THE USA MATTER MORE TO HIM THAN GOLF

Every now and again, we're given minor glimpses into the personal lives of these all-world athletes that remind us that we're all just humans who actually do have shared experiences, and nothing humbles anyone on a more consistent basis than raising kids.

For Scheffler last week, that humbling and relatable moment came in the form of hand, foot, and mouth disease. Following Sunday's final round in St. Louis, Scheffler revealed he had been battling the common childhood illness and the painful blisters that come with it throughout the BMW Championship.

Speaking to the media ahead of this week's PGA Tour finale, the Tour Championship, Scheffler was asked if it was at all humbling that his life away from the course sometimes impacts his life inside the ropes.

He took his time and delivered an imperfect answer, which, when it comes to talking about raising kids and a work-life balance, a perfect answer does not exist.

"Humbling is probably not -- not exactly how I felt. I feel like I've talked a lot about like I don't -- like I have -- it's almost like a double life essentially," Scheffler began.

"I have a life out here where I play and compete. When we're inside the ropes, it's definitely different than my home life. There's a lot of eyes on you. There's cameras like pretty much, let's say, six hours a day when I'm out here traveling...So when it comes to going home, I just go home, and I don't feel any different. I have my life out here where I play and compete, and I have my life at home where I don't really do a whole lot to be honest with you. It's not that exciting.

"We have a great group of friends at home that I love to see. I've got great family. When I think about the fall and our off-season, we don't really do a whole lot. Like you said, striking the balance between competing out here while also traveling with my family is something that I'm always trying to strike the balance because I work really hard at my sport and I'm trying to be the best husband, father that I can be.

"I think it's always a balancing act. I'm at a point in my life where, yeah, it's really hard having two young kids and taking care of them. I think anyone with young kids can relate, you're just tired literally all the time.

"I think you want to enjoy the season because eventually my kids aren't going to be able to be out here. It's something that I talked about with -- (Brian) Harman is somebody I talk a lot about this with. He's like, 'man, I'm jealous of you guys who get to travel every week with your kids.' You take the good with the bad. Part of it is hard, but part of it is you've got to also enjoy it because it doesn't last."

Here you have the best golfer walking the planet, who has earned over $20 million in less than nine months, dealing with the same everyday personal challenges every parent faces.

The balancing act of doing enough at work to provide, which Scheffler has accomplished given the commas in his bank account, but also giving it your all at home as a father is an unavoidable grind, both mentally and physically.

We're all just trying to get by the best we can, even the guy with a couple of green jackets in his closet.

item.title: Philadelphia DA says he'll keep piece of Trump's White House ballroom 'after we all blow it up'

The hikers, all adults traveling in four separate groups, became trapped around 2:30 p.m. Monday as floodwaters affected several popular trails, according to FOX 13 in Salt Lake City.

Following medical evaluations, two hikers showed signs of hypothermia and were taken to a hospital.

Those storms can create hazards including flash floods, trail washouts, debris-filled waterfalls and rockfalls, according to the park service.

item.title: Pumpkin spice invades summer as Americans kickstart fall traditions earlier than ever
item.description: Demand for pumpkin spice latte spiked two weeks earlier than 2021, and 49% of consumers now start Halloween shopping before October even begins.
item.content:encoded:
If it seems like fall décor and seasonal food and drinks are arriving earlier each year, it's not just in your head.

Data show consumers are increasingly embracing "season creep" — shopping for seasonal products earlier than they did in years past.

Younger consumers' enthusiasm for fall, a desire to plan ahead and retailers' efforts to extend seasonal spending may all be helping drive the shift.

STARBUCKS TO PROMPT MORE TIPPING ON CARD PAYMENTS, FUELING 'TIP CREEP' BACKLASH

Last year, the popular pumpkin spice latte (PSL) returned to Dunkin' on Aug. 20 and to Starbucks on Aug. 26. Both coffeehouse chains brought their fall offerings back a day earlier this year, with Dunkin' launching its fall menu on Aug. 19 and Starbucks bringing back its PSL on Aug. 25, Florida Today reported.

Data from online grocery delivery and pickup service Instacart showed that in 2024, "the seasonal peak for orders containing pumpkin spice items occurred on September 17, a full 10 days earlier than in 2023."

Demand also cooled sooner, according to Instacart, though orders for pumpkin spice items, such as flavored coffee creamers and yogurts, spiked again in November as Thanksgiving drew near.

Food delivery service DoorDash reported in 2025 that "pumpkin spice is brewing sooner than ever."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

PSL demand spiked on Aug. 19, nearly two weeks earlier than in 2021, the company reported.

DoorDash also found that grocery orders for ingredients used to make fall-inspired drinks at home began spiking in late July.

According to the National Retail Federation (NRF), 49% of consumers said in 2025 that they would begin shopping for Halloween before October, compared with 34% a decade earlier.

"More 18- to 24-year-old early shoppers say they look forward to fall or that Halloween is one of their favorite holidays, and they plan accordingly," the NRF reported. "Their early Halloween shopping isn't about 'impulse purchases,' but rather intentional planning ahead."

Younger shoppers were much more likely to say they wanted to avoid the stress of last-minute shopping for décor and costumes, according to the NRF survey.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Seasons affect people's minds and behavior for several reasons, Michael Varnum, professor and social psychology area head at Arizona State University, told Fox News Digital.

Some of these effects are physiological, such as the ways our bodies and hormones respond to changes in light, temperature and other climatic conditions throughout the year, he said.

The way seasons cause changes in illness, travel or population may also cue changes in how we think and act, Varnum noted.

"How we respond to seasons isn't purely driven by actual changes in the environment but is also shaped by other associations, traditions, rituals and schedules – spring break, back to school in fall, Halloween, Christmas, etc. – that are built into our society and what we learn from an early age," he said.

Climate and the environment also likely play a part, he said, reasoning that hotter summers could make people more eager for the cooler weather of fall.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Varnum said it's interesting that our culture's comfort in and enjoyment of seasonal traditions are heavily shaped by a model of four seasons "that doesn't necessarily fit well with what actually changes in the weather and environment in all parts of the world."

He also acknowledged that a big part of season creep may be driven by marketing.

"My guess is that retailers and others hope to capture boosts in spending associated with holidays or seasonal shifts earlier with the idea that it might extend the period for which they'll see it in their sales," he said.

He added that it would be "interesting to know whether such marketing might be more or perhaps less effective when there is more of a mismatch between the season being invoked and the actual weather or time of year."

Basically, picture yourself building a tower of cards or popsicle sticks only for someone to come and take away the foundation right as you're about to finish the job. The Cubs bullpen gave up five runs over the final two innings, losing the game. And Mason Miller, one of the best closers in baseball, allowed a run in a scoreless game to give the Pirates a win. Sometimes you can't dodge bad luck. Hopefully, I get some positive play in my favor now.

The Los Angeles Dodgers come into this one as just the second team in baseball to win 80 games. Although they will almost certainly win the National League West, they are still in a battle with the Brewers for the #1 overall seed in both the National League and the Majors. What is wild about the Dodgers is they aren't even playing with their best possible team. The pitching staff is finally looking a bit healthier than normal, but Will Smith is out, Kyle Tucker is playing poorly, Shohei Ohtani isn't pitching, and Dalton Rushing is also on the injured list. There is still another level the Dodgers can go to.

The roster might as well be an All-Star team, and this pitching staff is absurd. Tyler Glasnow is their fifth starter on the depth chart — he would be the first for probably about 25 other teams. Due to the injuries and conservation of the staff, the team throws a sixth starter, Roki Sasaki. He is one of the younger guys in the rotation, and someone who it seems like the Dodgers are still trying to figure out how to use. He was outstanding in the postseason for them last year. This season, in 22 starts, he is 5-5 with a 4.42 ERA and a 1.30 WHIP. He has pitched fairly well in August, but Braves hitters have been decent against him with three hits in just 11 at-bats.

The Atlanta Braves aren't too far behind the Dodgers, but they now must once again fend off the Phillies, who are hot on their tail. Two weeks ago, it felt like the Braves would coast to the postseason as the leaders in the National League East. Now they only have a 4.5-game lead, and most of that is due to the Phillies being hot, and less about the Braves struggling. However, over their last 10 games, the Phillies are 8-2, while the Braves are just 4-6. Still, the chances of either team missing the postseason are pretty low.

Looking to complete the series win over the Dodgers is AJ Smith-Shawver. For the season, Smith-Shawver has made only two starts, allowing six earned runs in 8.2 innings. He has walked five batters while giving up nine hits in that span as well, so there has been plenty of traffic on the base paths. This will be his first home start, and that could be a benefit to him as young guys might need that home crowd behind them. This is actually his fourth year in Major League time, so he has faced two Dodgers hitters and they are 2-for-7 against him. Alex Call is 2-for-5 with a double and triple.

The Braves have won the first game of the series, so if they can steal this one, they complete the series win of two teams that might end up in the National League Championship Series. It really doesn't mean much, but it would give Atlanta a little more confidence. I think this game likely sees some runs as both teams are gifted on offense and both pitchers look like they are more than willing to allow baserunners. I like the over 8.5 here. I also like the Dodgers to win the game. I'm playing the over, but I'll sprinkle the Dodgers money line as well.

item.title: Jelly Roll unleashes crude jokes about Trump's weight on 'Kimmel', 'from one fat pig to another'
item.description: Jelly Roll mocked Trump's weight and approval ratings while guest-hosting "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" using the Freedom 250 Grand Prix as material.
item.content:encoded:
Country music star Jelly Roll, who previously said he was not political, mocked President Donald Trump's weight, physical fitness and approval ratings Monday night in Los Angeles while guest-hosting "Jimmy Kimmel Live!", while using the president's appearance at Washington's Freedom 250 Grand Prix and recent physical as material for his opening monologue.

"Well, Mr. President, from one fat pig to another, take it from me that physical fitness is very important. And trust me, you’ll be happy to see your penis again," Jelly Roll said. "It’s crazy. Think about this, y’all. In the last few years, I’ve lost 300 pounds. That means I’ve lost an entire Donald Trump."

"And let’s be honest, based on his approval ratings, it seems like most of the country wants to do the same thing," he added.

Fox News Digital reached out to the RNC for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

TRUMP TAKES HONORARY LAP AROUND INDYCAR TRACK IN WASHINGTON AHEAD OF FREEDOM 250 GRAND PRIX

A Reuters/Ipsos survey released last week placed Trump at 33% approval and 64% disapproval, tying the lowest approval rating across both of his terms, Fox News Digital reported.

"President Trump has signed the largest middle-class tax cuts in history, lowered the cost of prescription drugs, sealed the border, driven violent crime to the lowest level in nearly a century, unleashed an energy revolution and sent Americans’ 401(k)s climbing to record highs," White House spokesperson Olivia Wales told Fox News Digital in response to questions about the polling.

"President Trump is cleaning up Joe Biden’s mess, and there is more work to do, but the United States of America has never been stronger," she continued.

Jelly Roll began the political portion of the monologue by discussing Sunday's Freedom 250 Grand Prix. Trump and first lady Melania Trump completed an honorary lap in the presidential limousine before the president waved the green flag to start the race, which Kyle Kirkwood won, according to OutKick.

TRUMP CALLS ON ALL FUTURE CANDIDATES TO TAKE COGNITIVE EXAM, NOTING PERFECT SCORE DURING LATEST PHYSICAL

"The president seemed to enjoy the IndyCar race, which was a real switch up for him, because normally he only likes his own race," Jelly Roll said.

He joked about the reaction to his previous Trump quips on Tuesday night's "Kimmel" show, saying he couldn't believe he would have "stunned" anyone with Trump jokes.

"Some folks online were upset that I didn't treat the president with reverence and dignity," he said. "But I want to remind y'all that I go by the name Jelly Roll. I don't even treat myself with reverence and dignity."

He added the president should be able to "handle a few jokes."

"I get it that some people are mad at me for goofing on Trump, but if you wanted me to make jokes about Kamala Harris, you should have voted for her," he said.

TRUMP MARKS 80TH BIRTHDAY, NOW SECOND OCTOGENARIAN SITTING PRESIDENT: 'SEEMED TO UTTERLY DEFY AGE'

The monologue marked a rare political turn for Jelly Roll, whose real name is Jason DeFord. After the Grammy Awards in February, he declined to offer an immediate opinion about the country’s political climate and questioned why people would seek his views, Fox News Digital reported.

"You know, I’m a dumb redneck. Like, I haven’t watched enough. I didn’t have a phone for 18 months," Jelly Roll said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

His Monday remarks also differed from his response after meeting Trump at UFC 309 in 2024, when the then-president-elect told Jelly Roll that he liked his song "Save Me." Jelly Roll defended the encounter and said his family taught him to honor the office regardless of its occupant.

Jelly Roll first guest-hosted "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" in July 2025 and returned this week while Kimmel was on his summer break.

Fox News Digital's Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this story.

item.title: Green New Dodge: El-Sayed runs from policy as newly surfaced deleted posts show years of support
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed refused to defend the Green New Deal on air, but deleted posts show he once wrote "I believe in a Green New Deal" in all caps.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed told Fox News host Jesse Watters on Monday that he would not defend the Green New Deal when confronted with his past support for the progressive climate proposal, a notable shift from years of publicly embracing it by name.

"Look, I’m not going to defend the Green New Deal," El-Sayed told Watters after the host confronted him over his past support for the proposal. When Watters reiterated that El-Sayed was on record supporting it, El-Sayed redirected the discussion toward lowering energy costs and creating Michigan jobs by prioritizing renewables.

Michigan, which Trump won in 2024 but lost in 2020, is shaping up to have one of the most competitive Senate races in the country, with the likely narrow results in the state potentially determining control of Congress. Critics charge that El-Sayed is downplaying some of his past beliefs and scrubbing his online footprint to appear more moderate, and therefore more palatable, to Michigan voters.

UNEARTHED CLIP EXPOSES MORE ANTI-POLICE RHETORIC AS EL-SAYED GETS GRILLED FOR DELETING SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS

Though El-Sayed declined to defend the Green New Deal in front of a national audience, he previously hasn’t been so shy.

A Fox News Digital review of El-Sayed's deleted social media posts, preserved via the Internet Archive, uncovered dozens of examples of the Michigan Senate hopeful defending the Green New Deal by name.

"Rather than announcing the next iteration of this or that car at [the North American International Auto Show 2019], I’d love to see automakers announce that they support the #GreenNewDeal," El-Sayed wrote in January of that year.

On the primary campaign trail, Rep. Haley Stevens criticized El-Sayed over his past support for the Green New Deal on the grounds that it could lead to job losses in the automobile manufacturing industry.

FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS: AS DEMOCRATS TURN LEFT, BLACK VOTERS TAP THE BRAKES

"The struggle for the Green New Deal uplifts the struggle for racial justice," El-Sayed wrote in April 2019.

The Green New Deal is a 2019 progressive policy framework floated by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., that seeks to gradually transition the United States’ electrical grid away from fossil fuels. Their plan has become synonymous with the left-wing faction of the Democratic Party, leading many Democrats running in competitive races to distance themselves from it.

In another post, from September 2019, El-Sayed wrote, "I believe in a Green New Deal" five times in all caps. He also suggested that the Green New Deal is essential to preserve freedom of speech because there can be no First Amendment "without the freedom to breathe the breath you have to take to speak in the first place."

"The #GreenNewDeal doesn’t center polar bears or glaciers, it centers those children forced to breath (sic.) in corporate pollution in their communities," El-Sayed wrote. "I stand with the Green New Deal because it stands for those kids."

WATCH: SURFACED VIDEOS OF DEM SENATE CANDIDATE BACKING 'DEFUND THE POLICE' CONTRADICT RECENT DENIALS

CNN previously reported that El-Sayed scrubbed large swathes of his commentary from the internet prior to announcing his run for Senate. The deletions appear to have been selective, as he still has some posts up from before he launched his campaign.

In his since-deleted social media posts, El-Sayed endorsed the "defund the police" movement, argued cities spent too much policing poverty and described police departments as "standing armies we deploy against our own people." In a separate YouTube video that was later hidden, he floated replacing the Second Amendment’s right to bear arms with a constitutional right to healthcare and called Border Patrol agents "white supremacists" while blaming American policies for migration from struggling nations.

Though El-Sayed regularly mentioned the Green New Deal on X prior to running for Senate, he has not posted the phrase even once since announcing his candidacy, a review found. 

The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

item.title: Texas law targeting drag shows could have criminalized the late Dolly Parton, judge ruled
item.description: Judge David Hittner blocked Ken Paxton from enforcing Texas Senate Bill 12, citing First Amendment protections for drag shows and free speech.
item.content:encoded:
A Texas law targeting drag show performances was struck down for the second time Tuesday by a Reagan-appointed judge who ruled that the law's "broad" language could even be applied to banning performances by Jennifer Lopez, Miley Cyrus and the now late Dolly Parton.

Gov. Greg Abbott signed Senate Bill 12 into law in June 2023, which prohibits "sexually oriented performances" from occurring in public places or where someone under 18-years-old may be present.

The law imposed up to a $10,000 fine on business owners for hosting drag show events. Performers at the events could have also been charged with a class A misdemeanor.

At the time, Abbott dubbed the law a ban on public drag performances on social media, prompting a lawsuit filed by LGBT organizations, entertainment groups and a drag queen performer. The lawsuit accused the law of being in violation of first speech rights.

IOWA TEACHERS SUSPENDED OVER VIRAL STUDENT-RUN DRAG SHOW REACH SETTLEMENT BEFORE TRIAL

U.S. District Judge David Hittner ruled that the law can not stand because it is "unconstitutionally vague" and  "fails to give a reasonable person notice of what is prohibited," suggesting that any entertainers with sexual undertones in their performance could be penalized.

"Just as many people criticized Elvis’s signature hip gyrations and were offended by his display of male sexuality, chastised Dolly Parton as a voluptuous sex symbol because of her big hair, flamboyant clothes and breast exposure, and shamed Miley Cyrus for ‘twerking’ on stage during a live performance at the 2013 MTV Video Music Awards, there are ‘erotic’ elements in countless popular performances that could be subject to both civil and criminal penalties under S.B. 12," Hittner wrote.

GEORGIA PRIDE GROUP RECRUITING KIDS AS YOUNG AS 13 INTO DRAG SHOWS SPARKS BACKLASH

Hittner first struck down the law in September 2023 on five constitutional grounds, but while Texas’s appeal was pending, the Supreme Court issued its 2024 decision in Moody v. NetChoice, clarifying how courts must evaluate facial First Amendment challenges. The 5th Circuit Court of Appeals handed the case back down with further instructions on how to decide the case based on precedent set in the Moody decision. 

GOP LAWMAKERS URGE SUPREME COURT TO STRENGTHEN FIRST AMENDMENT PROTECTIONS FOR STREET PREACHER

Hittner again found the law unconstitutional, offering advice for those against drag shows.

"For those who find such activities as described in this case offensive, the solution is relatively simple ... just don't go," Hittner wrote in his briefing. 

The Texas law sought to justify its ban on the claim that drag shows appeal to "the prurient interest," but Hittner brushed that claim aside, ruling that state law doesn't define what "prurient interest in sex" means.

"Because S.B. 12 does not specify who determines whether a performance ‘appeals to the prurient interest,’ or require that the work be taken as a whole, a single moment of eroticism could condemn an entire performance to criminal or civil penalties," Hittner wrote.

"There are ‘erotic’ elements in countless popular performances that could be subject to both civil and criminal penalties under S.B. 12," he wrote, going on to list "cheerleading, dancing, live theater, and other common public occurrences," as activities that could be banned under the law.

SEATTLE PRIDE PARADE PANDEMONIUM AS NUDE MARCHERS PRANCE THROUGH STREETS IN FRONT OF CHILDREN

Hittner immediately and permanently barred Attorney General Ken Paxton from enforcing the law and denied Paxton’s request for a new trial and additional discovery. However, Paxton, who is running for U.S. Senate, is able to appeal and said he intends to do so.

"This is a profoundly flawed decision that endangers our children and is an affront to Texas values," Paxton wrote on X. "I will appeal this decision immediately and continue to fight to protect our kids."

Fox News Digital reached to Paxton and Abbott's office for comment.

Drag performer Brigitte Bandit, a plantiff in the lawsuit, celebrated the ruling. Bandit's performances include impersonations of Dolly Parton, who passed away at 80-years old on Tuesday.

"Drag has always been a form of free expression, and it is a relief that the court recognized that today," Bandit said in a statement . "We use our performances to assert liberation, power, and joy with our community. As a lifelong Texan, I’m sick of this state trying to censor art and stoke hatred and violence against drag artists and the LGBTQIA+ community."

The ruling comes weeks after a federal appeals court approved a Florida law restricting children from sexually explicit performances, including many drag shows.

The Florida law defines an "adult live performance" as a live show that "depicts or simulates nudity, sexual conduct, sexual excitement, or specific sexual activities ... lewd conduct, or the lewd exposure of prosthetic or imitation genitals or breasts" and that also predominantly appeals to a "prurient, shameful, or morbid interest," is "patently offensive" for the age of the child present and, taken as a whole, lacks serious literary, artistic, political or scientific value for that child's age.

item.title: The ultimate dog-friendly road trip on Minnesota's North Shore from Duluth to Grand Marais
item.description: From Split Rock Lighthouse to Pincushion Mountain, a dog-friendly road trip reveals why Minnesota's North Shore demands more than three days.
item.content:encoded:
A few weeks ago, I set out with the intention of writing an itinerary for the ultimate dog-friendly vacation on the Minnesota North Shore. Turns out, that's not as easy as I thought.

Not for a lack of writing material, either.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

No, the challenge I ran into was that I couldn't fit all the outdoor adventures the area had to offer into the measly three days I planned to visit.

Not a bad problem to have.

Every summer, my husband and I visit my mother-in-law at her snowbird summer home in Minocqua, Wisc. During that trip, we like to take a few days to drive up to Lake Superior and see what kind of hiking we can find. In 2024, we explored the Porcupine Mountains in Michigan's Upper Peninsula. Last year, it was the Apostle Islands at the tippy top of Wisconsin.

YOU DON'T NEED A KAYAK TO APPRECIATE NORTHERN WISCONSIN'S APOSTLE ISLANDS

This year, we figured we'd try Minnesota.

So I booked us a little Airbnb right on the lakeshore in Tofte, we threw our packs, our boots and our German Shepherd in the truck, and away we went.

Admittedly, before this trip, I knew nothing about the stretch of land between Duluth and the Canadian border — aside from the fact that it's very cold in the wintertime, and I imagined every guy up there probably looked something like the Brawny Man. So I relied on my old friend Google (and my very helpful Nightcaps readers) to build our itinerary.

Did you know there are eight state parks in that 150 miles of shoreline? EIGHT. So I knew we, sadly, weren't going to hit them all on this trip. We'd have to pick a few and save the rest for next year.

At least a couple dozen people told me I had to go to Betty's Pies in Two Harbors — an iconic little café that's been around for 70 years. They have, I'm told, the best pies in all of Minnesota. Maybe all the Midwest. And like an idiot, I didn't listen.

Instead, our first stop was at Iona's Beach. Which was delightful, too.

Iona's Beach is a cute little crescent-shaped shore in Two Harbors that, instead of sand, is covered by salmon-colored pink rocks. In other words, this is not the sort of beach where you stroll barefoot. The stones are pink because they're made of rhyolite, a rock formed from ancient volcanic activity.

The area is named after a sweet little old lady named Iona Lind, whose family originally owned the land and ran the resort that used to stand where the parking lot is now.

Supposedly, the pebbles make a "singing" sound as Lake Superior's waves shift them back and forth against each other. But if I'm being honest, they just sounded like regular rocks to me.

Still, Iona's Beach is worth your time for a quick stroll and some photos along the shore.

Next up, we hit Split Rock Lighthouse.

A couple of things to note about Split Rock Lighthouse:

After hitting the Tofte General Store beer-bait-barbecue-and-tackle shop (not what it's called, but it should be) for some food to cook, we headed to our Airbnb.

Friends, when I tell you it was like stepping back in time, I mean it. This particular property was built in the early 1970s and almost certainly has not been updated since. Our particular condo, though, had a 90s vibe — complete with an impressive collection of VHS tapes. We're talking "Liar Liar," "A Few Good Men," "Forrest Gump," "Titanic"! All the hits.

But we didn't choose this rental for the decor. We chose it because it's located smack on the top of a cliff overlooking Lake Superior. The kind of view that makes you want to pop open a bottle of wine, sit down in an Adirondack chair and just stare into the horizon.

And you best believe that's what I did.

We planned Wednesday to be our big hiking day. But first, a quick stop to check out the giant rock formation they call Palisade Head. It's a 300-foot granite cliff created in the Ice Age, and it's a seriously cool challenge for rock climbers.

Or you can take the easier route like we did. Park your car in the designated viewing area and admire Palisade Head from afar. While we were there, we made conversation with a couple of dudes who proceeded to list all the cool hiking spots we needed to check out during our trip to the North Shore. It was at this moment I realized I should have scheduled out more than three days.

HERE’S HOW TO DO THE SMOKY MOUNTAINS WITHOUT TRAFFIC AND CROWDS

From there we headed to Tettegouche State Park. I kept pronouncing it "Tet-uh-GOOCH-ee" (à la "way down yonder on the Chattahoochee.") However, a sign in the visitor center informed me the correct pronunciation is "TET-uh-goosh."

Bummer.

There are roughly 23 miles of hiking trails in Tettegouche, so we hopped on AllTrails and created our own adventure: Shovel Point to High Falls to Two Step Falls. I think we made the right choice.

Our route took us out to the lake shore, down along the river, to an incredible swimming hole at the base of High Falls, through some woody terrain and into a peaceful little lunch spot on the stream at Two Step. It worked out to about 6.2 moderate miles with multiple spots for Rocky to hop in the water and cool off.

High Falls was the star of the show.

On our way back to the condo, we decided to drive up Oberg Mountain. The loop gave us stunning vistas and a really cool overlook of Oberg Lake. I was pretty tired after Tettegouche, but this was well worth the extra 2.5 miles.

That night we headed up to Moguls Grill & Taproom for post-hike burgers and beers. It's inside the Caribou Highlands Lodge, which serves as a ski resort in the wintertime. Dogs aren't allowed inside the restaurant, but we snagged some food to go and sat out on the patio.

There, we met a nice elderly lady named Patrice who said she comes to the North Shore a few times a year "to escape the far-left hell scape of Minneapolis."

Those fellas up on Palisade Head told us we have to check out the Gunflint Trail.

So much great hiking on the Gunflint Trail! Beautiful country! Such cool wildlife! I see moose all the time!

I do not love the idea of running into a grumpy moose out on the trail. But their sales pitch got me.

Upon further research, though, I discovered the Gunflint Trail is actually a 57-mile byway that stretches all the way from the lakeshore into the Boundary Waters and damn near to Canada. Since we didn't budget enough time to cover all that ground, we chose the very first trail off the Gunflint: Pincushion Mountain.

On the way up US 61, though, we stopped at a local coffee shop called Fika that came highly recommended by our Airbnb host.

Holy cow, you guys, are you familiar with maple syrup lattes? Because they are, I learned, very much a thing in northern Minnesota.

Now listen, I drink my coffee like my grandpa does: strong, black and by the bucket. One step short of jet fuel. But what's the point of driving 16 hours from home if you don't try the local fare?

My goodness. That maple syrup latte was worth every bit of the (probably) 500 calories it cost me. What a concept. Consider it fuel for the 5.75-mile Pincushion Mountain Loop.

Half of this trail was on an old logging road, which the curmudgeonly reviewers on AllTrails didn't love. I swear people on AllTrails will complain about everything.

The grass was too tall in some places. I had to step over a log. A bug landed on my shoulder!

You're in the woods, Sharon.

That said, the logging road portion of this trail was a little boring, but that's fine. Because the payoff was an epic view of Lake Superior and Grand Marais from the top of a massive bald monolith.

Pro tip: Make sure you veer off this loop to check out Barrier Falls. We went down to the bridge at West Devil Track before turning around and heading back to the loop.

The climb out of there was a bit of a b----, but suck it up, buttercup. You've got a maple syrup latte to burn off.

After this hike, we walked around Grand Marais — a charming little harbor town. We stopped by the Gunflint Tavern for lunch. But heads up, it is not dog friendly except for the upstairs bar, which does not serve food. It does, however, serve the Fulton 300 IPA, which is 10/10 if you're into that sort of thing.

If you find yourself in Grand Marais, do yourself a favor and make the windy walk out to the lighthouse. I can't believe I'm saying this, but it was so cold out there that I cursed myself for not bringing a beanie. In July!

Grand Marais is just about 35 miles to the Canadian border. However, my husband and I did not go to Canada. Because we are PATRIOTS.

Just kidding. It's because both of our passports are expired. But we plan to remedy that soon.

On our way out of town, we noticed Voyageur Brewing Company. It looked like a fun spot, and I wish we would have known about it ahead of time. They have a blonde ale that's very popular around these parts.

One cool thing about the North Shore is that everything is right off US 61. You really can't get lost. So on our way back to Tofte, we stopped for a quick 1-miler at Cascade River State Park.

This is an easy little trek — even after you enjoyed a beer or three in Grand Marais. Ask me how I know.

The next morning, I set my alarm for 5 a.m. so that I could catch the sunrise. With a perfectly east-facing condo right on Lake Superior, it'd be criminal if I didn't drag my butt up for one sunrise.

And, friends, it was so, so worth it.

On our way back to Minocqua, we popped in Coho Cafe & Bakery. No exaggeration — the best pancakes I'd ever tasted in my life. Absolute perfection.

As we enjoyed our breakfast, we plotted next year's adventure. Grand Portage, Thunder Bay, Devil's Kettle, the Summit Express gondola up Lutsen Mountain, the Boundary Waters. All the things we just didn't have time for this year. And all dog friendly.

Truthfully, we fell in love with Grand Marais. That seems like an obvious base camp for the 2027 Great White North adventure.

And I promise — this time — we're hitting Betty's Pies.
